season|2010]], [[2010–11 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|2011]]) * Third-team All-ACC (2009) | bbr = delanma01 }} '''Malcolm Hakeem Delaney''' (born March 11, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He is from [[Baltimore, Maryland]], and attended [[Towson Catholic High School]]. Delaney played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball]] team. At the end of his college career, Delaney declared for the [[2011 NBA draft]]. He was not drafted, and instead began his professional basketball career overseas, playing one season each for [[Élan Chalon]], [[BC Budivelnyk|Budivelnyk Kyiv]], and [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]], and later joined [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] for two seasons. In [[2015–16 Euroleague|2016]], he earned an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] selection. ==Early life== Delaney was born in [[Baltimore|Baltimore, Maryland]] on March 11, 1989. His mother Patricia was a nurse and [[day care]] provider. His father Vincent Jr. was a top high school basketball player in Baltimore and later became a starter at [[Voorhees College]] in [[Denmark, South Carolina]].{{cite web|title=Malcolm Delaney Bio|url=http://www.hokiesports.com/mbasketball/players/delaney_malcolm.html|website=HokieSports.com|access-date=December 1, 2016}} Vincent Jr. returned from college as a social worker.{{cite web|last1=Fairbank|first1=Dave|title='There's something about Baltimore guards'|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2010/11/06/theres-something-about-baltimore-guards/|website=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|access-date=December 1, 2016|date=November 6, 2010}} Malcolm's older brother Vincent played [[NCAA Division II]] college [[American football|football]] for [[Stonehill College]] in [[Easton, Massachusetts]]. In his childhood, Delaney led his [[Pop Warner Little Scholars|Pop Warner]] youth football team to the national title. He also won a [[Little League Baseball]] home run derby. At age seven, Delaney dribbled and shot balls on the sidelines at an [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team practice.{{cite web|last1=Kilgore|first1=Adam|title=McClinton, Delaney Share Baltimore Ties|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/02/08/AR2008020803804.html|website=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=December 3, 2016|date=February 9, 2008}} ==High school== Delaney first attended [[McDonogh School]] in [[Owings Mills, Maryland]], where he played football and basketball.{{cite web|last1=O'Malley|first1=Pat|title=MIAA grants basketball transfer waiver|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2004/09/03/miaa-grants-basketball-transfer-waiver/|website=[[Baltimore Sun]]|access-date=December 3, 2016|date=September 3, 2004}} He started for the Eagles' basketball team and helped them see great success during his freshman season. McDonogh most notably defeated [[Mount Saint Joseph High School]], the top-ranked team in the [[Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association]] (MIAA). Delaney also guided the Eagles to wins over ranked [[Cardinal Gibbons School (Baltimore, Maryland)|Cardinal Gibbons School]] and [[Towson Catholic High School]].{{cite web|last1=O'Malley|first1=Pat|title=Curley's first and only baseball coach, Frank retires after 41 years|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2004/02/07/curleys-first-and-only-baseball-coach-frank-retires-after-41-years/|website=[[Baltimore Sun]]|access-date=December 4, 2016|date=February 7, 2004}} Before his sophomore year, Delaney transferred to Towson Catholic, where he continued to play MIAA basketball under head coach Josh Pratt. He joined fellow sophomores [[Donté Greene]] and Ron Nicholson on the Owls' roster.{{cite web|last1=Telep|first1=Dave|title=On the Road: Towson Catholic|url=http://www.scout.com/college/rutgers/story/322649-on-the-road-towson-catholic|website=[[Scout.com]]|access-date=December 4, 2016|date=November 24, 2004}} He averaged 20 points, four rebounds and four steals as a senior. Also played in the Nike All-American All-Star game and was co-MVP of the Spalding Hoopball Classic. Was an EA Sports second-team All-American, Charm City Classic MVP, [[Capital Classic (all-star game)|Capital Classic]] All-Tournament team and Baltimore Catholic League Player of the Year. Delaney earned Gatorade Player of the Year/Mr. Maryland and was an All-County selection as a senior. At Towson Catholic, led team to the Baltimore Catholic League and MIAA Championships as a senior and scored 2,112 career points. Delaney was the No. 89 ranked player in the country and No. 13 ranked point guard according to Rivals. He received offers from Virginia Tech, Clemson, Indiana, Iowa State and Maryland. He also played for AAU Team Melo and is friends with former New York Knicks star and Maryland native [[Carmelo Anthony]]. He committed to the Hokies on September 3, 2006. ==College career== ===Freshman year=== [[File:Malcolm Delaney Virginia Tech.jpg|thumb|right|150 px|Delaney with [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] in 2011]] Delaney finished second on the team in assists (107, 3.1 apg), fourth on the team in scoring (9.6 ppg) and minutes played (27.3) and fifth on the team in rebounding (2.9 rpg). He started the last 24 games of the season and appeared in all 35 games. He scored in double figures in all three Virginia Tech post-season games. He registered a career-high 20 points and tied a career-high in steals, with four, at UNC. He made the game-tying three-pointer with 52 seconds remaining against Maryland in the home victory. ===Sophomore year=== In his second season Delaney was named third-team All-ACC. He scored more than 20 points in 12 games and more than 15 points in 25 contests. Improved his scoring average and was second on the team in scoring, averaging 18.2 ppg. He was ranked among the ACC leaders in scoring (6th, 18.1 ppg), assists (5th, 4.5 apg), free throw percentage (3rd, 86.9%) and minutes played (2nd, 36.5). Delaney led the Hokies with 14 points and a career-high-tying 10 assists in the loss to Baylor in the second round of the NIT. He won the Lou Carnesecca Award, given to the most valuable player of the Aeropostale Holiday Festival, after averaging 23.5 ppg, 6.5 rpg, 6.0 apg and 3.0 spg for the tournament. ===Junior year=== In his junior year Delaney was a unanimous first-team All-ACC after recording a career-best 20.2 ppg for the season.[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=5172292 Virginia Tech's Malcolm Delaney returning for senior year - ESPN] He led the Hokies to the [[National Invitational Tournament|NIT]] quarterfinals and had 24 points in their season-ending loss to Rhode Island. Led the ACC in scoring and was the Sporting News' fourth-team All-America selection. Delaney led the ACC in trips to the free throw line and imparted his knowledge to teammate Dorenzo Hudson who made a career-high 20 free throws on 21 attempts in their victory over Seton Hall. ===Collegiate statistics=== {|class="wikitable" |- !Year !Games Played !Minutes/Game !Points/Game !Rebounds/Game !Assists/Game !Steals/Game !Steals/Season |- |2007–08 |35 |27.3 |9.6 |2.9 |3.1 |0.8 |28 |- |2008–09 |34 |36.9 |18.1 |4.0 |4.5 |1.5 |50 |- |2009–10 |33 |35.8 |20.2 |3.7 |4.5 |1.2 |41 |- |2010–11 |34 |38.2 |18.7 |3.5 |4.0 |1.6 |56 |} ===2010 NBA draft=== Delaney entered the [[2010 NBA draft]] on March 31, 2010, but did not hire an agent.{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/05/01/AR2010050102955.html |title=NCAA basketball non-seniors have smaller window to declare for NBA draft |work=Washingtonpost.com |date=2010-05-02 |access-date=2014-03-17}} He had until May 8 to withdraw from the Draft or forgo his senior season. On May 7, Delaney decided to return to the Hokies for his senior season. On ESPN he had been projected as a second round draft choice to undrafted.{{cite web|url=https://insider.espn.com/nbadraft/results/player/_/id/79355/malcolm-delaney |title=Malcolm Delaney 2011 NBA Draft Profile - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=1989-03-11 |access-date=2014-03-17}} ==Professional career== ===Élan Chalon (2011–2012)=== In 2011, after going undrafted, Delaney signed with the French team [[Élan Chalon]] in an agreement worth $130,000.{{cite web|last=Giannotto |first=Mark |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/hokies-journal/post/malcolm-delaney-has-deal-in-place-to-play-in-france-if-he-goes-undrafted-in-nba/2011/06/21/AGy6vNeH_blog.html |title=Malcolm Delaney has deal in place to play in France if he goes undrafted in NBA - Hokies Journal |work=The Washington Post |date=2011-06-21 |access-date=2014-03-17}} The team plays in France's top professional league, [[LNB Pro A]]. In his first professional game, Delaney recorded 12 points and 8 assists in a 77–73 win over [[BCM Gravelines-Dunkerque|BCM Gravelines]].{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/France/2011/1008_878_341.asp|title=Elan Chalon 77 - BCM Gravelines 73|publisher=Eurobasket|date=October 8, 2011|access-date=January 20, 2020}} On April 6, 2012, Delaney recorded his first career double-double after racking up 30 points and 10 assists in a 99–109 overtime loss to the [[Nanterre 92|Nanterre]].{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/France/2012/0406_878_2347.asp|title=Elan Chalon 99 - Nanterre 109|publisher=Eurobasket|date=April 6, 2012|access-date=January 20, 2020}} ===Budivelnyk Kyiv (2012–2013)=== In 2012, Malcolm Delaney agreed to a deal to play for [[BC Budivelnyk]] in Kyiv, Ukraine. The club plays in the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/ukraine/42196/budivelnyk-officially-signs-delaney-and-salenga.html |title=Budivelnyk officially signs Delaney and Salenga |publisher=Sportando.net |date=2012-08-08 |access-date=2014-03-17}} He was named to the [[EuroCup Basketball All-EuroCup Team|All-EuroCup First Team]] in 2013.{{cite news|title=Star power fills 2012-13 All-Eurocup teams!|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/111934/star-power-fills-2012-13-all-eurocup-teams|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119204047/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/111934/star-power-fills-2012-13-all-eurocup-teams|url-status=dead|archive-date=January [[Basketball Bundesliga MVP]] award.{{cite web |url=http://www.schoenen-dunk.de/news_a69001_FC-Bayern-Muenchen_Der-MVP-heisst-Malcolm-Delaney.htm |title=SD | News | FC Bayern München | Der MVP heißt German basketball champions|German League title]] by beating [[Alba Berlin]] 3–1 in the Finals, and Delaney won the [[Basketball Bundesliga Finals MVP|Finals MVP]] award. ===Lokomotiv Kuban (2014–2016)=== On July 2, 2014, Delaney signed a one-year deal with the Russian team [[PBC Lokomotiv Kuban]].{{cite news|title=Lokomotiv Kuban inks proven winner Delaney|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/138329|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714132401/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/138329|url-status=dead|archive-date=July web|last1=Bi|first1=Rakesh|title=Exclusive Interview with Malcolm Delaney, Overseas Basketball Star|url=http://theleaguenews.us/exclusive-interview-with-malcolm-delaney-overseas-star/|website=TheLeagueNews.us|access-date=8 December 2014}}{{cite web|title=Lokomotiv Kuban officially signs Malcolm Delaney|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/125363/lokomotiv-kuban-officially-signs-malcolm-delaney.html|website=Sportando.com}} In the summer of 2015, he re-signed with Lokomotiv for 2015–16 season.{{cite news|title=Kuban president confirms Delaney, Randolph and Balashov will remain|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/171208/kuban-president-confirms-delaney-randolph-and-balashov-will-remain.html|access-date=July 31, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=July 31, 2015}} He led his team to the [[2016 EuroLeague Final Four]] where Lokomotiv finished in third place. Delaney averaged 16.3 points, 5.5 assists and 3.4 rebounds over 31 [[2015–16 Euroleague|EuroLeague]] games. ===Atlanta Hawks (2016–2018)=== On July 15, 2016, Delaney signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]]{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/features/hawks-re-sign-humphries-add-jack-delaney|title=Hawks Re-Sign Humphries, Add Jack & Delaney|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}} on a 2-year, $5,000,000 deal. He made his NBA debut in the Hawks' season opener on October 27, 2016, recording four points and five assists in 20 minutes off the bench in a 114–99 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899420|title=Wizards vs. Hawks – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=October 27, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2017}} On February 24, 2017, in a 108–90 loss to the [[Miami Heat]], Delaney had five points and four assists and made only 2 of 10 shots from the field in his first career start as a fill-in for [[Dennis Schröder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900269|title=Tyler Johnson leads resurgent Heat past Hawks, 108-90|work=ESPN.com|date=February 24, 2017|access-date=February 25, 2017}} === Guangdong Southern Tigers (2018–2019) === On July 28, 2018, Delaney signed with the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).{{cite web |title=Guandong Tigers add Delaney to their roster |url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/541604/Guandong-Tigers-add-Delaney-to-their-roster |publisher=Asia-Basket |access-date=July 28, 2018 |date=July 28, 2018}} In his first game with the Southern Tigers, he recorded 19 points, 5 rebounds and 3 assists in a 87–84 win over the [[Beijing Ducks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2018/1021_1943_941.asp|title=Guangdong Southern Tigers 87 - Beijing Ducks 84|publisher=EuroBasket|date=October 21, 2018|access-date=February 5, 2020}} ===FC Barcelona (2019–2020)=== On September 12, 2019, Delaney signed a one-year deal with an option for another season with [[Liga ACB|Spanish]] [[EuroLeague]] powerhouse [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]].{{cite news |title=Barcelona lands former All-Euroleague guard Delaney |url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9xmhjur546pu4hsf |access-date=12 September 2019 |work=[[EuroLeague|EuroLeague.net]] |date=12 September 2019}} In his first game with FC Barcelona, Delaney racked up 8 points, 4 rebounds and 6 assists in a 92–86 win over the [[Obradoiro CAB|Obradoiro]].{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/Spain/2019/0927_1348_100.asp|title=Obradoiro CAB 86 - FC Barcelona 92|publisher=EuroBasket|date=September 27, 2019|access-date=February 5, 2020}} He averaged 10.2 points and 3.7 assists per game. In May 2020, FC Barcelona released Delaney from his contract.{{cite news |title=Malcolm Delaney, Barcelona part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/malcolm-delaney-barcelona-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 2, 2020 |date=May 14, 2020}} ===Olimpia Milano (2020–2022)=== On June 2, 2020, Delaney signed a two-year contract with [[Olimpia Milano]] in [[Lega Basket Serie A|Italy]].{{cite web |title="Happy and excited to be part of this project": Malcolm Delaney is coming to Milan |url=http://www.olimpiamilano.com/en/happy-and-excited-to-be-part-of-this-project-malcolm-delaney-is-coming-to-milan/ |publisher=olimpiamilano.com |date=2 June 2020 }} On October 17, he was ruled out at least 20 days after suffering a left ankle sprain.{{cite news |title=Milan's Malcolm Delaney out at least 20 days with ankle sprain |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/milans-malcolm-delaney-out-at-least-20-days-with-ankle-sprain/ |website=Sportando |access-date=October 17, 2020 |date=October 17, 2020}} On May 12, 2022, Delaney mutually parted ways with the Italian club, having already suffered a season-ending injury. Afterwards, he stated that the 2022 season would be his last season with any European basketball team or club.{{cite web|last=Kyriakidis|first=Giorgios|url=https://basketnews.com/news-167701-malcolm-delaney-this-will-be-my-last-full-season-in-europe.html|title=Malcolm Delaney: 'This will be my last full season in
